_: ENV-3 · the declared migration state of each environment.
This file is NOT a ledger. supabase_migrations.schema_migrations is the ledger
and the only authority on what IS applied. This file declares what SHOULD be
applied where, so CI has something true to compare the ledger against.
The comparison is two-way, exactly as known-violations.json is: a version
applied without being declared here fails, and a version declared here without
being applied fails. The frontier can only move when reality and intent move
together.
Semantics, and there are only four rules:
applied_through  the frontier. Expected = every authored version <= this,
minus anything in `excluded`.
excluded         authored versions AT OR BELOW the frontier that are
deliberately not applied here. Each needs a reason and the
gate that releases it.
pending          authored versions ABOVE the frontier, deliberately not yet
applied. Each needs a reason and the gate that releases it.
every authored version must appear in exactly one of those three states.
Silence is not a state -- an undeclared migration fails.
Only QA is declared. Production's history is reconciled by RELEASE_GATES row
9B.2 (G-09), which owns dumping and reconciling its ledger and enumerates its
known divergences in 9B.3. Declaring a production frontier here before that
work exists would be inventing state this repository cannot yet stand behind.

186.reason: Restores the coach programme engine. Migration 124 left the public materialize_program_week delegating to an engine that still holds 093's body: with an empty intelligence substrate it writes days with 0 exercises and reports success; with a populated one it fails 23514 (the canonical-prescription CHECK). 186 replaces only materialize_program_week_engine: 119's canonical prescription (sets/reps from context, default 3x10, weight_kg null, full day names), all-or-nothing (every session validated before any write; ENGINE_NO_SELECTION changes nothing), no silent overwrite (an existing week is replaced only with replace_existing = JSON true; ENGINE_WEEK_EXISTS otherwise), malformed sets/reps refused (ENGINE_BAD_PRESCRIPTION), and a FOR UPDATE lock on the programme so concurrent calls cannot duplicate a week. Wrapper, signature and authorization (124, can_act_on_program) unchanged; engine stays revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated. Locally replay-verified: supabase/tests/local/engine_materialize_replay.sh, 28 checks — 8 PASS / 20 FAIL on 000-181, 28/28 with 186 on 000-181 and on 000-185+186; a two-session concurrency test serialized correctly. 197.reason: A coach assigns only a program the coach owns. 199.reason: Storage writes need ownership. exercise-media (061, public): write/update/delete checked only bucket_id, so any signed-in user -- a client included -- could upload, overwrite or delete every exercise's media. coach-media (036, public): any signed-in user could upload, write into another coach's folder, and list/sign coach-videos/<coach>/<client>/... Replaces those policies with rules that mirror existing authority: exercise-media paths must name an existing exercise; writers are an admin, the private exercise's coach, or (platform exercise) a coach or admin as update_exercise_media (072) allows; delete is admin or the private exercise's coach. coach-media writes stay in the uploader's own folder (coach/admin), adding the missing own-folder UPDATE; videos read only by their coach and client. update_exercise_media now also requires the owner or an admin on a PRIVATE exercise. Buckets stay public (product/infra decision). Locally replay-verified: storage_199_replay.sh 14 FAIL before / 29 of 29 after, also on QA's shape. NOT applied to QA.
199.gate: An owner-approved QA apply window naming 199, then the live QA suites and CI. Before any controlled-beta exercise media or coach media is introduced.
